The Fremouw Formation can be subdivided into three informal members. The lower member consists of coarse to medium-grained, trough cross-bedded, channel-form sandstone units alternating with equally thick fine-grained units of fine to very fine-grained sandstone, silstone and mudstone . - Institute of Polar Studies Report 87.

The Fremouw Formation can be subdivided into three informal members. The middle member, which is relatively nonresistant and generally poorly exposed, is dominated by fine-grained sandstone, siltstone and mudstone units that are interbedded with relatively thin medium-grained, channel form and tabular sheet sandstone units. - Institute of Polar Studies Report 87.

The Fremouw Formation can be subdivided into three informal members. The upper member consists of coarse to medium-grained slope-forming, channel-forming sandstone alternating with fining-upward sequences of very fine-grained sandstone, siltstone and mudstone. - Institute of Polar Studies Report 87.

The Lashly Formation was subdivided into informal members (A, B, C and D) in Barrett, P.J. and Kohn, B.P. (1975) Changing sediment transport directions from Devonian t o Triassic in the Beacon Supergroup of south Victoria Land, Antarctica In: Campbell, K.S.W. (Ed.), Gondwanan geology. Canberra, Australian National Univ. Press, pp. 329-332.

Lashly member C consists of fining-upward cycles of medium- to fine-grained sandstone grading upward into carbonaceous siltstone and mudstone, and thin coal beds. Quartz pebbles and cobbles and mudstone clasts occur near the base of major sandstone units. Irregular lenses of coal occur along bedding planes and over large scours. Dicroidium fronds and other plant fragments are common in carbonaceous beds.

Tavener-Smith (1960, 1962) and Gair (1960) divided the Madumabisa Mudstone Formation into three units, Lower, Middle and Upper, considering that the lower and upper units are more homogeneous and poorly stratified compared to the middle unit, which contains numerous calcilutite layers and concretions that contain fossils.

Another persistent stratum of flinty lime, the Burnt Fork White Layer, lies about the middle of the horizon. Fossils abundant and varied. The Lower to Upper Permian Buckley Formation is divisible into upper and lower members based on sandstone composition and paleocurrent orientations. The lower member consists of arkosic sandstone that was deposited by streams flowing off the craton and axially down the basin toward the present Weddell Sea (figure 1, block d). In the upper Buckley, sand-stone composition changes abruptly from arkosic to volcani-clastic. Concommitant with the influx of volcaniclastics was a 180 degree reversal in paleocurrent orientations (Collinson and Isbell 1986).

Named as series by Hill (1887) for its development along the coastal plain of the Gulf of Mexico. Subdivided into (in descending order): Basal Tertiaries (Marine Tertiary), Navarro beds, Dallas limestone, Eagle Ford shales, and Timber Creek group. Includes Middle Cretaceous and Upper Cretaceous strata.
